_provenance: Category assumptions are analyst-INFERRED (see products-clusters.md Section 9), not product facts. Each is linked only to real evidence (research corpus, real product distribution stats) that genuinely bears on it - evidence lists are empty where no real source in this session's corpus addresses that specific assumption.

assumptions.text: Purification requires a dedicated, standalone box.
assumptions.evidence_for_prevalence: 170 of 237 real corpus products (72%) are classified standard_purifier - a single dedicated appliance is still the dominant real architecture.
assumptions.evidence_note: RP-04 shows floor-level resuspension is a real, distinct spatial dynamic a stationary box doesn't directly address - opens the question without proving an alternative wins.
assumptions.counterfactual: What if purification were distributed across several small nodes instead of one box?

assumptions.text: The device sits in one fixed location, chosen once.
assumptions.evidence_for_prevalence: No real product in this corpus is marketed as mobile or multi-room by design.
assumptions.evidence_note: RP-01 shows a purifier's benefit already leaks unevenly beyond its own room; RP-04 shows a real spatial source (walking) the fixed box doesn't chase.
assumptions.counterfactual: What if the device (or its effect) followed the person, not the room?

assumptions.text: The consumer reacts after pollution is measured, not before.
assumptions.evidence_for_prevalence: 162 of 237 products (68%) are cluster_intelligence=manual; only 8 are adaptive.
assumptions.evidence_note: RP-09/RP-10 show current sensors are precise-but-not-always-accurate - a real constraint on how confidently any product could act predictively today.
assumptions.counterfactual: What if the product acted on a forecast, not a measurement?

assumptions.text: Filters are replaced manually by the consumer.
assumptions.evidence_for_prevalence: "filter_cost" is a real, distinct consumer-complaint theme in the taxonomy (0.26% prevalence, real evidence) - replacement friction is a lived reality.
assumptions.evidence_note: No paper in this session's research corpus addresses filter-subscription or auto-replacement models - this counterfactual has no direct research backing, only the real consumer-complaint signal.
assumptions.counterfactual: What if the consumer never has to remember, buy, or touch a filter?

assumptions.text: Clean-air delivery rate (CADR) is the primary performance basis.
assumptions.evidence_for_prevalence: ENERGY STAR and AHAM certification (TC-R02, TC-R03) both center CADR as the official performance metric.
assumptions.evidence_note: RP-07 explicitly reports a discrepancy between theoretical CADR-based sizing and measured performance; RP-06 shows raw real-world averages can mislead entirely; RP-01 shows single-room CADR doesn't capture whole-home effect. Real evidence directly challenges CADR as sufficient, not just as a label.
assumptions.counterfactual: What if performance were reported as a loss-rate curve or realized exposure reduction, not a lab CADR number?

assumptions.text: Continuous, constant operation is the default expectation.
assumptions.evidence_for_prevalence: Standard purifier control panels default to a fixed or continuous mode; only 15 of 237 products are classified connected, and 8 adaptive.
assumptions.evidence_note: RP-07's own trial shows constant mode filters 66% vs. auto's 40% - constant is not neutral, it's a real trade-off against noise/runtime; RP-05 shows noise measurably suppresses real usage.
assumptions.counterfactual: What if the operating mode were chosen per household noise tolerance, not shipped as one default?

assumptions.text: The consumer owns the hardware outright after a single upfront purchase.
assumptions.evidence_for_prevalence: All 237 real corpus products are sold as one-time purchases on Amazon - no subscription/service model observed in this corpus.
assumptions.evidence_note: No paper in this session's research corpus addresses ownership models - this is a pure category-structure observation, not backed by the peer-reviewed corpus.
assumptions.counterfactual: What if clean air were sold as a guaranteed outcome/subscription rather than a device?

assumptions.text: A visible interface or app is required to trust the product is working.
assumptions.evidence_for_prevalence: 15 of 237 products explicitly market app/voice connectivity as a selling point.
assumptions.evidence_note: If the underlying sensor reading itself carries real, documented uncertainty (RP-09, RP-10), a more prominent display doesn't fix the trust problem - it may just surface an unreliable number more confidently.
assumptions.counterfactual: What if the most trustworthy product had no visible number at all, only a confidence-qualified state?
